# Introduction: 
```{r, Read the data, echo=FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(readr)
CHD <- read_csv("~/Desktop/RSPH/Fall2026/DATA550/Final/Data/framingham.csv")
```
The Coronary heart disease data set has `r nrow(CHD)` rows and `r ncol(CHD)` columns from an ongoing cardiovascular study on residents of the town of Framingham, Massachusetts. Including some demographics, behavioral and medical conditions that might contribute to a future coronary heart disease (CHD)

## Goal of the analysis:
1. Understand the potential risk factors contributed to coronary heart disease (CHD)
2. Classification prediction based on the statistically significant independent factors and the dependent outcome 

# Descriptive Analysis

## Tabular analysis
### Table 1
```{r, table1, echo=FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(labelled)
library(gtsummary)

var_label(CHD) <- list(
  age = "Age of the patient",
  BMI = "Body Mass Index",
  totChol = "Total cholesterol level",
  glucose = "glucose level",
 heartRate = "Heart Rate",
 sysBP = "systolic blood pressure",
 diaBP = "diastolic blood pressure"
)

CHD$Gender <- ifelse(CHD$male == 1, "Male", "Female")

CHD |>
  select("Gender","heartRate", "age", "sysBP", "diaBP", "totChol", "glucose", "BMI") |>
  tbl_summary(by = Gender, missing = "no") |>
  modify_spanning_header(c("stat_1", "stat_2") ~ "**Summary of CHD**") |>
  add_overall() |>
  add_p()
```
Table 1 is a simple summary of the data, containing the following variables:
Age of the patient, BMI, Total cholesterol level, glucose level, Heart Rate, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure. Divided onto two groups by gender.
There is some similarity of most of the variables between male and female, except the BMI, where it was slightly higher among male. 

## Graphical analysis
### scatter plot
```{r, Scatter_plot, echo=FALSE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| fig.align = "center",
#| out.width = "400px"
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(CHD, aes(x = heartRate, y = BMI)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = lm) +
  theme_bw()

```
The above graph shows a distribution of the heart rate and the BMI, in addition to the regression line close to 25.4 (23.1, 28.0) in BMI.
